headline: This law lets the Treasury Department mint up to 400,000 silver dollar coins honoring women who helped win the 19th Amendment, with sale profits going to the Smithsonian.
what_it_does: The law directs the Treasury Department to mint and issue up to 400,000 one-dollar silver coins. The coins are meant to honor women who helped build support for the 19th Amendment, which gave women the right to vote. The coins could be issued only during calendar year 2020. Surcharges collected from coin sales go to the American Women's History Initiative at the Smithsonian Institution.

who_it_affects.how: They can buy the silver dollar coins while they are offered for sale in 2020, and the price includes a surcharge.

who_it_affects.group: The Smithsonian Institution's American Women's History Initiative
who_it_affects.how: It receives the surcharge money collected from coin sales.

who_it_affects.group: The U.S. Treasury Department and U.S. Mint
who_it_affects.how: They must produce and issue the coins within the set limit and time period.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on November 25, 2019. Coins may be issued from January 1, 2020, through December 31, 2020.
